finding.claim: [High] For MariaDB servers, TLS certificate validation is disabled and the native-password scramble is sent before the fingerprint check. An on-path attacker presenting any non-authorized certificate receives a password-derived scramble (offline-crackable; potentially relayable to the real server).
finding.source: On-path attacker presenting an untrusted/self-signed/hostname-mismatched certificate to a client using default ssl options against a MariaDB server; seed is in the plaintext greeting.
finding.sink: Handshake.send writes the native auth token to the socket (handshake.js:134-162, flush at :215).

trace.note: requireValidCert = true under default ssl options
MariaDB: baseConf.rejectUnauthorized forced to false
TLS socket created with forced rejectUnauthorized=false
TLS callback runs with untrusted peer
selfSignedCertificate = !authorized (true for attacker cert)
sole guard: blocked only if !isMitmProof()
Handshake.isMitmProof returns true for non-clear plugins, so guard does not fire
native plugin declares itself MITM-proof
Handshake.send invoked before any server validation
native scramble computed from attacker-supplied seed
token flushed to attacker-controlled TLS socket
fingerprint validation only happens on the later OK packet (validateFingerPrint at handshake.js:215-244)

finding.guards_checked: requireValidCert/selfSignedCertificate flags (present but gated on isMitmProof, which is true for native); isMitmProof guard at handshake.js:67; requireSecure (clear-password only); restrictedAuth (undefined by default, authentication.js:272); auth-switch re-check at authentication.js:308-321 (also passes for native); fingerprint validation (runs after send, authentication.js:77-98).

finding.claim: [Medium] pool.escape() passes null connection info when no idle connection exists, forcing backslash escaping; under NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES the output is injectable.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled string passed to pool.escape(value); precondition: server sql_mode includes NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES and the pool has zero idle connections.
finding.sink: SQL literal built by application from pool.escape() output (utils.js escapeString -> literal).

trace.note: escape(value) -> Utils.escape(connOptions, this._searchInfo(), value)
_searchInfo: idle queue get(0) checked first
active lookup iterates Object.keys indices, not threadIds
lookup of '0','1',... in #activeConnections (keyed by threadId, see pool.js:493,560) returns undefined
break -> info stays null
escapeParameters default branch -> escapeString(null, value)
noBackslashEscapes = info != null && ... evaluates false
backslash-mode regex selected
quote escaped as \' (backslash), injectable under NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES

finding.guards_checked: connection.escape binds live info (connection.js:112) so it is not affected; escapeId does not depend on mode; wire-path writers do honour the mode (packet-output-stream.js:549-574) but pool.escape string path does not; Buffer path with null info throws TypeError (utils.js:130-133), a crash rather than injection.

finding.claim: [Medium] Server-supplied redirect_url causes the client to open a new connection to an arbitrary host and reuse the original password.
finding.source: redirect_url in OK-packet session-state tracking, controlled by the server (requires a CA-trusted certificate or a compromised database host).
finding.sink: new Connection with Object.assign({}, this.opts, redirectOpts), carrying this.opts.password to the redirect target.

trace.note: redirect_url read from session-state tracking of OK packet
info.redirect(value, ...) invoked
delegates to connection.redirect
gate: this.opts.permitRedirect && value
permitRedirect default = true when ssl enabled and rejectUnauthorized !== false
target host/port taken from server-supplied URL
user/password replaced only if present in URL; otherwise original password retained
Object.assign merges this.opts (including password) into redirect options
new Connection connects to attacker-chosen host with the original credentials

finding.guards_checked: permitRedirect default gate (connection-options.js:114-117); same-host skip (connection.js:2099-2102); protocol allowlist mariadb/mysql only (connection.js:2084); not-in-transaction check (connection.js:2076); no host allowlist and no user confirmation; fingerprint path returns before redirect handling (authentication.js:93-95).

finding.claim: [Low] Compressed packets from the server are inflated synchronously with no output cap; a small compressed payload can expand to a very large buffer (client memory exhaustion).
finding.source: Server-controlled compressed packet payload (malicious server or on-path peer when compress option is enabled).

trace.note: unCompressLen parsed from header
branch taken when unCompressLen != 0
inflateSync(chunk) with no maxOutputLength; declared unCompressLen never checked against actual output
packetLen computed from header but never enforced as a cap

finding.guards_checked: compressed packet length limited to 0xffffff per chunk (compression-input-stream.js:111,117) but output size is unbounded; no maxOutputLength option.

finding.claim: [Low, policy] Credentials (clear-text password, native auth scramble) and query parameter values are written to the configured logger when debug logging or a logger is enabled, contrary to the org rule against logging passwords.
finding.source: Application enabling debug: true or supplying a logger; logParam defaults to true.
finding.sink: opts.logger.network / opts.logger.query (hex dump of handshake packet; displaySql with parameters).

trace.note: logParam defaults to true
query logged with displaySql (parameter values) when logger.query set
mysql_clear_password: plaintext password written into handshake response
native scramble written into handshake response
out.flushPacket() on handshake response
flushPacket -> flushBuffer (debug variant when debug enabled)
flushBufferDebug logs hex of first debugLen (default 256) bytes, which contain the password for typical lengths

finding.guards_checked: debug and logger are opt-in (connection-options.js:37-67); debugLen truncates to 256 bytes but still includes credentials for typical user/password lengths.

finding.claim: [Low] Cluster pattern cache is a plain object keyed by attacker-influenced strings; inherited keys like 'constructor' or '__proto__' are returned as cached node lists, and the cache is unbounded. RegExp(pattern) also compiles arbitrary patterns (ReDoS).
finding.source: Application passes request-derived string as a cluster pattern (getConnection/remove).

trace.note: _getConnection -> _matchingNodes(pattern)
#cachedPatterns[pattern] truthy for inherited Object members
RegExp(pattern) compiled from input
cache written with no size bound; '__proto__' assignment mutates prototype chain of cache object
remove(pattern) compiles RegExp(pattern) from input as well

finding.guards_checked: pattern required for remove() (cluster.js:83); no key validation, no cache bound, no use of Object.create(null) or Map.

finding.claim: [Low] changeUser overwrites the stored connection password with the per-call value while leaving the stored user unchanged, so later redirects reuse a mismatched user/password pair.
finding.source: Application calls changeUser({user, password}) or changeUser({user}) with no password.
finding.sink: connOpts.password mutation; later redirect creates connection with this.opts.

trace.note: per-call opts merged into this.opts (copy)
connOpts.password = cmdOpts.password (persisted on the connection)
redirect builds options from this.opts, including the mutated password

finding.guards_checked: none; user field is not persisted, so credential pair can diverge.

finding.claim: [Low, unverified] Prepared-statement cache is not cleared after COM_CHANGE_USER and is keyed without the user, so cached statement ids may refer to statements the server has released (or reused).
finding.source: Application calls changeUser after preparing statements on the same connection.
finding.sink: prepareCache.get -> execute with cached statement id.

trace.note: changeUser path: no prepareCache.reset() in success callback (1678-1699)
only reset() clears the cache
cache key = database|sql, no user component
cache hit reuses statement id

finding.guards_checked: database component in key (lru-prepare-cache.js:42); no user component; server-side behaviour on statement-id reuse after COM_CHANGE_USER not verified.
